chunks: Muhammad ibn Al-Qasim al-Isterabadi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to me from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him).

He said: When Gabriel brought the news of the death of al-Najashi to God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he cried bitterly for him and said, 'Your brother, whose name is al-Najashi, has died.' Then he went out to Al-Jabbana and said 'Allahu Akbar' seven times. Then God lowered every elevated place for him until he saw his corpse, and he was in Ethiopia.

key_terms.الْجَبَّانَةِ: A specific area in Medina used for funeral prayers

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do upon hearing the news of al-Najashi's death?
ai.summary: This tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Prophet’s deep affection for the righteous Christian king of Abyssinia, whom he affectionately called 'Aṣḥamata' (our brother). The miraculous lowering of the hills to allow the Prophet to view the body in Ethiopia underscores the spiritual proximity of the righteous across geographical and religious divides, a key theme in Shia hagiography regarding the universality of divine mercy.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-19 Muhammad ibn Al-Qasim al-Isterabadi - may God be pleased with him - quoted on the authority of Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father (s), on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (s), on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (s) that

God’s Prophet (s) said, “When Gabriel brought the news of the death of al-Najashi to God’s Prophet (s), the Prophet (s) cried very hard for him and said, “Your brother whose name is al-Najashi has died.” The Prophet (s) then went to the desert and said ‘Allahu Akbar’ seven times. Then God evened out all the hills for him so that the Prophet (s) could see al-Najashi’s corpse in Ethiopia.”
